newsitem.title: USA: Sealright sees Q1 costs offset by sales.
newsitem.headline: Sealright sees Q1 costs offset by sales.

text.p: Sealright Corp, which is consolidating its operations to be more efficient, said Monday it sees only minimal restructuring costs in 1997 and expects those expenses to be offset by the sale of closed facilities.
Sealright noted that all of these expected 1997 costs will occur in the first quarter. The amount was not disclosed.
Sealright designs and makes packaging for consumer products companies.
Earlier, the company reported a 1996 fourth quarter loss of $7.3 million or $0.66 a share due to charges from restructuring activities and discontinuing an operation.
Sealright is selling its Los Angeles, Calif., rigid plastic packaging business and consolidating its North Carolina flexible packaging operations in other Sealright plants.

Sealright said it agreed to sell the North Carolina plant to Butler and Smith Inc, a packaging company, and expects to complete the sale by March 31. It also has contracts or letters of intent to sell three vacant facilities in the Kansas City area. Terms were not disclosed.
These actions should position the company for much better results in 1997, Sealright said in a statement.
Sealright also said its restructuring plan has generated margin improvements that will return as production volumes increase.

In other developments, Sealright said its customer partnerships are generating new sales in 1997. The company has had a relationship with Dreyer's Grand Ice Cream Inc, which produces Healthy Choice frozen desserts for ConAgra Inc . As a result of the relationship, Sealright said it will provide all Healthy Choice half-gallon packaging.
Also because of a new long term agreement with McCormick and Co, Sealright said it will be the sole supplier to all U.S. McDonald's Corp stores for dispensed-sauce packaging used for condiments.
The agreement with McCormick initially is worth more than $2 million in additional sales.
